synthesis.original_text: Would tripling trastuzumab's half-life maintain HER2 occupancy longer than improving its binding affinity tenfold?

answer.statement: The simulation cannot show which intervention keeps HER2 occupancy above threshold longer because all three scenarios remain above threshold when the 120-day window ends, so duration is censored. Endpoint occupancy is higher for the threefold longer half-life than for tenfold stronger affinity, and occupancy AUC is also higher for the half-life change.

missing_evidence.statement: Observed human tumor HER2 occupancy over time to validate model predictions.
Clinical efficacy and safety data linking occupancy duration to outcomes.
In vivo validation of apparent SPR kinetics at body temperature for effective HER2 sites.

simulation_implications.statement: Endpoint occupancy is higher with a threefold longer half-life than with tenfold stronger affinity through slower dissociation.
Occupancy AUC is higher with a threefold longer half-life than with tenfold stronger affinity through slower dissociation.
All three scenarios remain above the 90% occupancy threshold at the end of the 120-day window, so time above threshold is censored and cannot distinguish duration.

limitations: Simulated occupancy is a conditional prediction of the stated PK and binding model; it is not evidence of clinical efficacy, safety or an appropriate regimen.
